original_question: On graphs more complicated than a star graph, such as trees or graphs with loops, can one build an orbital-stability or orbital-instability theory for nonlinear standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation when explicit formulas for the standing waves are unavailable? In particular, can one effectively count negative eigenvalues of the linearized operator and verify the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition in these less explicit graph geometries?
target_in_paper: The closest paper-faithful target is the open-problem paragraph at the end of Section 2.3, immediately after Theorem 4, where Noja asks whether the orbital stability/instability analysis available on star graphs can be extended to more complex graphs (for example, trees or graphs with loops) and notes that, without explicit standing waves, directly counting negative eigenvalues of the relevant selfadjoint linearized operator and checking the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition becomes impossible or at least very difficult. citeturn20view0turn14view2
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual intent. It correctly identifies: (i) the move from star graphs to more complex graph topologies such as trees and graphs with loops; (ii) the goal of an orbital stability/orbital instability theory for standing waves of NLS; (iii) the fact that the star-graph case is easier because explicit stationary states are known; and (iv) the two technical bottlenecks singled out by the paper, namely counting negative eigenvalues and checking the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition. citeturn20view0turn14view2
missing_details: The paper's question sits inside the focusing NLS standing-wave setting on metric/quantum graphs, not arbitrary nonlinear waves: standing waves are of the form e^{i\omega t}\Phi and satisfy the stationary graph equation discussed in Section 2.1. citeturn14view2turn15view0

The open problem is specifically about extending the Weinstein/Grillakis-Shatah-Strauss framework used in Section 2.3, where orbital stability is defined modulo the phase orbit and is tied to spectral conditions plus the Vakhitov-Kolokolov slope condition. citeturn6view0turn20view0

The relevant spectral quantity is the Morse index of the selfadjoint operator appearing in the second variation/linearization of the action, not just 'the linearized operator' in a loose sense. citeturn20view0

The nearby context narrows the question to regular branches of standing waves, especially branches predicted by bifurcation theory when the underlying quantum graph has an eigenvalue, for example the linear ground state. citeturn20view0turn22view0

A stand-alone formulation should make clear that this is the first of two nearby open problems in the paragraph; the second, distinct problem is how to obtain branches of bound states without a linear counterpart. citeturn20view0

The paper does not ask for a theory on all graph geometries uniformly; it says that some simple non-trivial graphs may be treatable, while more generally the direct analysis becomes very hard once explicit formulas are unavailable. citeturn20view0turn14view2
If one wants the stability notion to be fully stand-alone, one should say that orbital stability is meant in the graph energy norm/orbit sense of Definition 2.1. citeturn6view0
refined_question: For the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a metric/quantum graph more complicated than a star graph—for instance a tree or a graph with loops—and for a regular branch of standing waves e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega, especially one arising by bifurcation from an eigenvalue of the underlying quantum-graph Hamiltonian, can one extend the Weinstein/Grillakis-Shatah-Strauss orbital stability/instability analysis used on star graphs to the non-explicit setting, by determining the Morse index (the number of negative eigenvalues of the relevant selfadjoint operator in the linearization/second variation of the action) and by verifying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov slope condition along the branch? citeturn20view0turn14view2
justification: This paper has no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 matching your template. The nearest official formulation is the closing open-problem paragraph of Section 2.3 after Theorem 4. Theorem 4 and the preceding discussion provide the exact scope: standing waves of focusing NLS on graphs, orbital stability in the sense of Definition 2.1, and the GSS-type criteria via spectral conditions/Morse index and the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition. The paragraph then explicitly asks whether a similar analysis can be carried out on more complex graphs such as trees or graphs with loops, and explains that the hard step is precisely the direct verification of those criteria when explicit standing-wave formulas are unavailable; it also places this in the context of branches suggested by bifurcation from a linear eigenstate of the underlying quantum graph. citeturn20view0turn14view2turn6view0turn22view0
